headline: Ben's perfect week vaults him into second; Orest blanked
dek: Ben's 2-0 climbs him to within a game of Chris, who also went undefeated. Four head-to-heads decided, with Orest suffering the week's only 0-2.
takeaways: Four head-to-heads resolved in Week 6 — the most consequential being Ben over Matej in Houston, flipping two points in the standings
Chris maintains the pool lead at 9-3 but Ben's perfect week brings him within a game, and Ben holds a whopping +40 edge in net points
Taras' Chargers are now 0-6 after another ugly showing in Kansas City — they've been outscored by 84 points in six games

games.text:
Jordy's Broncos escaped with a low-scoring head-to-head win over Orest's Seahawks in Denver, 17-14. Bo Nix managed just 107 yards through the air but J.K. Dobbins punched in a rushing touchdown to provide the margin. Sam Darnold threw for 278 yards but couldn't find the end zone, tossing two costly interceptions instead. Jaxon Smith-Njigba hauled in 12 catches for 134 yards in a losing effort.

The result flips a point in Jordy's favour and keeps his Broncos at 4-2, while Orest's Hawks slide to 3-3. Jordy took the only bye-free 1-0 this week and sits in fifth place with 7 points. Orest, meanwhile, is staring down an 0-2 weekend and drops to fourth at 7-5.

Ben's Texans held off Matej's Jags in a wild shootout in Jacksonville, 34-31, in the week's highest-scoring head-to-head. C.J. Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns, while J. Noel torched the Jags secondary for 107 yards and a score. Trevor Lawrence kept Jacksonville in it with 306 yards and four touchdowns of his own, but it wasn't quite enough.

The win pushes Ben to 2-0 on the week and vaults him into sole possession of second place at 8-4, just one game behind Chris. Ben's Niners remain undefeated at 6-0, and even his struggling Texans managed a road win to improve to 2-4. Matej takes the loss and drops to 0-2 for the week, falling to sixth at 6-6. He'll need his Eagles to turn things around quickly.

Orest's Ravens stumbled in Cleveland, falling 13-10 in a defensive slugfest. Deshaun Watson threw for just 164 yards but avoided major mistakes, while backup Tyler Huntley couldn't generate much for Baltimore with only 165 yards through the air. Derrick Henry managed 58 yards on the ground but couldn't find the end zone.

The loss completes a dismal 0-2 week for Orest, who sees both his teams fall in Week 6. His Ravens drop to 4-2 but remain competitive in the AFC, while his Seahawks' loss to Jordy's Broncos leaves them at 3-3. Orest sits fourth in the pool at 7-5, watching Ben and Tymko close in from behind.

Adrian's Patriots got a breakout performance from rookie Drake Maye, who threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns in a 26-19 win over the Jets. Demario Douglas caught seven balls for 86 yards and a score, while Geno Smith threw for 252 yards on the other side but couldn't keep pace.

The win salvages Adrian's week at 1-1 after his Bucs fell to Bill's Steelers. His Patriots improve to 4-2 and look increasingly dangerous with Maye under center, though his Bucs remain a disaster at 1-5. Adrian sits eighth at 5-7, needing his Patriots to carry the load the rest of the way.

Taras' Panthers rolled into Philadelphia and dominated Matej's Eagles, 25-14, in a head-to-head that wasn't as close as the score suggests. Chuba Hubbard gashed the Eagles defence for 120 yards and a touchdown on 28 carries, while Bryce Young connected on two touchdown passes. The Eagles' backup quarterback Trevor McKee threw for 215 yards and a score but couldn't generate much offense.

The win gives Taras a 1-1 split and his Panthers improve to 3-2, providing a rare bright spot in his otherwise miserable season. Matej, meanwhile, completes an 0-2 disaster as both his teams lost head-to-heads this week. His Eagles fall to 2-4 and his Jags dropped a shootout to Ben's Texans. He's now 6-6 and falling fast.

Bill's Steelers escaped Tampa with a 26-19 head-to-head victory over Adrian's Buccaneers. Aaron Rodgers aired it out 49 times for 253 yards and two touchdowns, with DK Metcalf hauling in 11 catches for 93 yards. Jayden Daniels struggled mightily for the Bucs with just 164 yards and two interceptions in a losing effort.

The win gives Bill a 1-1 split on the week after his Cowboys were dismantled by Chris' Packers. His Steelers improve to 4-2 and remain in the AFC playoff hunt, while his Cowboys sink to 2-4. He sits seventh at 6-6. Adrian's Bucs, now 1-5, are becoming a serious anchor — they've lost to Bill's Steelers in a game they desperately needed.

Tymko's Rams came agonizingly close but fell at home to Arizona, 18-16. Matthew Stafford threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns, connecting with Puka Nacua six times for 80 yards, but the offense stalled when it mattered most. The Cardinals' ground game controlled the clock with running back Ben Knight racking up 80 yards.

The loss damages what could have been a perfect week for Tymko, who splits 1-1 after his Chiefs demolished Taras' Chargers. His Rams drop to 2-4 and look increasingly lost, while his undefeated Chiefs roll on at 5-0. Tymko sits third at 7-4, tied with Jordy but well ahead on net points.

Tymko's Chiefs absolutely throttled Taras' Chargers in Kansas City, 22-6, in a head-to-head that was never competitive. Kenneth Walker III ran wild for 128 yards and two touchdowns, while Patrick Mahomes efficiently managed the game with 272 passing yards. Justin Herbert and the Chargers managed just 204 yards through the air and couldn't crack the end zone once.

The win gives Tymko a 1-1 split after his Rams fell to Arizona, and his Chiefs remain the only undefeated team in the pool at 5-0. Taras, meanwhile, watches his Chargers drop to an abysmal 0-6 after being outscored 22-6. His Panthers won earlier in the week to salvage a 1-1 split, but the Chargers are dragging him down badly — he's dead last at 3-8.

Chris' Bills survived a back-and-forth thriller in Las Vegas, escaping with a 33-30 victory. Josh Allen threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns, while James Cook III bulldozed his way to 95 rushing yards and another score. Kirk Cousins kept the Raiders in it with 313 yards and two touchdowns, but it wasn't enough in the end.

The win completes a perfect 2-0 week for Chris, who maintains his pool lead at 9-3. His Bills improve to 5-1 and look like a legitimate contender, while his Packers also won to move to 4-2. Chris holds a one-game lead over Ben and is the only entrant still above .500 on both teams.

Chris' Packers dismantled Bill's Cowboys at Lambeau Field, 23-13, in a head-to-head that was never in doubt. Jordan Love threw for 276 yards and a touchdown to Malik Golden, who had 104 receiving yards. Dak Prescott struggled badly with 258 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions as the Cowboys' offense sputtered.

The win seals a 2-0 week for Chris and keeps him atop the pool standings at 9-3. His Packers improve to 4-2 and his Bills are 5-1 — he's the clear leader with both teams playing well. Bill takes the loss and finishes 1-1 on the week, with his Cowboys falling to 2-4 and looking increasingly hapless. He's seventh at 6-6 and needs his Steelers to carry more weight.

Ben's Niners stayed perfect with a 23-17 home win over Washington, improving to 6-0 on the season. Brock Purdy was efficient with 264 yards and a touchdown, while Christian McCaffrey punched in two rushing touchdowns on 64 yards. Jayden Daniels threw for 300 yards and two scores for Washington but couldn't overcome San Francisco's balanced attack.

The win completes a perfect 2-0 week for Ben, who vaults into second place in the pool at 8-4. His Niners remain the only undefeated NFC team in the pool and have been his lifeline all season. Even his struggling Texans won a head-to-head over Matej's Jags, giving Ben serious momentum heading into Week 7.

Next week his Eagles host Bill's Cowboys on Monday night in another head-to-head he desperately needs.
